title: Epochal reservation runway and opportunistic deferral controller
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce an epochal reservation runway (ERR) and opportunistic deferral controller to provide predictable throughput guarantees for Dedicated tenants while preserving short-burst capacity and graceful degradation when the fleet is under pressure.
background: Current Dedicated routing provides static reservations and a best-effort slowpath. Customers ask for firm short-term throughput guarantees with lower operational overhead than strict hard-isolation. We need a mechanism that: 1) converts monthly/committed capacity into time-windowed reservations (epochs) to allow better packing; 2) allows controlled, observable short bursts above steady guarantees via a rate cushion; and 3) defers non-latency-critical requests opportunistically when the fleet is saturated to protect critical SLAs.
proposal: Implement an Epochal Reservation Runway (ERR) that allocates each tenant a rolling reservation budget expressed in epoch-seconds. The controller maintains three pieces: a reservation runway (committed tokens per epoch), a rate cushion (short-lived borrowable slack computed from fleet headroom and pricing tiers), and an opportunistic deferral policy (delay queue with tenant-scored deferral priority and credit decay). Admission decisions consult ERR state: if within runway -> accept; if within cushion -> accept and mark as borrowed; if neither -> attempt deferral into the delay queue with tenant-specific timeout and fallback to shed or downgrade to cheaper model. Integrate with autoscaler hints so long-running runway exhaustion triggers scaled-up provisioning signals with TTL-based commitments.
design_decisions: We adopt epochal windows (default 60s) rather than per-request tokens to simplify accounting and reduce coordination cost. The rate cushion is computed at fleet shard level as a percentage of idle GPU capacity minus a safety buffer; higher-tier customers receive higher cushion ratios. Delay queue entries are tenant-scored by (sla_weight, recency, customer_tier) to favor committed customers. We will keep the initial implementation centralized in the admission proxy to avoid cross-shard synchronization complexity; subsequent iterations may surface per-shard local heuristics. This favors correctness and observability but increases risk of single-point performance bottleneck; mitigation includes sharded proxy instances and local caching of runway snapshots.
tradeoffs: Pros: predictable, burst-tolerant guarantees; improved utilization; explicit signals for autoscaling. Cons: added complexity in billing and debugging; central runway coordination may add latency; potential for unfairness if cushion policy mis-tuned. We choose gradual rollout plus tenant-visible metrics to manage tuning.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag behind runtime and console toggle; 2) Canary 5% traffic on dev/staging; 3) Pilot with 3 volunteer customers (non-critical workloads) for 2 weeks; 4) Expand to 25% with monitoring and circuit breakers; 5) Full release gated on SLA stability and billing audit. Each stage includes kill-switch and immediate fallback to existing admission policy.
metrics: Reservation fulfillment rate (per-tenant % of accepted requests within runway); borrowed-cushion utilization (%) at fleet and tenant level; delay-queue length and mean deferral time; percent of requests shed; tail latency (p95/p99) for in-runway vs borrowed vs deferred requests; autoscaler-trigger frequency and time-to-upscale; customer-facing availability and observed throughput vs committed throughput.
test_plan: Unit tests for runway accounting, cushion computation, and deferral priority. Integration tests: synthetic multi-tenant load with traffic mixes (steady, bursty, tail heavy) to validate guarantees and graceful degradation. Chaos tests: simulate shard loss and delayed autoscaler responses to verify fallback and shed paths. End-to-end billing reconciliation test to ensure borrowed cushion is tracked for surcharge or metric labeling.
acceptance_criteria: 1) ERR must maintain per-epoch booking with <1% accounting drift under 10k req/s; 2) Under 2x baseline burst, top-tier customers must see <5% shed rate for at least 30s; 3) Delay queue must not increase mean request latency for in-runway traffic by >10ms p95; 4) Autoscaler hints triggered within 120s of sustained runway depletion in pilot; 5) Dashboard surfaces all required metrics and exposes tenant runway/cushion state.
